ru.title: Разрешение на работу
ru.content: A foreign work permit is an authorization document issued by the Ministry of Labour and Social Security that foreign nationals must obtain to work in Türkiye. To obtain a work permit, applications must be made in accordance with the procedure and the appropriate work permit type must be identified. Otherwise, applications may be rejected. If an application is rejected, the foreign national has the right to object or bring an annulment action.

ru.title: Что такое разрешение на работу?
ru.content: A work permit is an official document issued by the Ministry of Labour and Social Security that grants the foreign national both the right to work and the right to reside in Türkiye for its period of validity. Under the International Labour Force Law, a permit must be obtained before starting dependent or independent work in Türkiye. Otherwise, working at any workplace in Türkiye is unlawful and carries sanctions.

ru.title: Как получить разрешение на работу?
ru.content:
A work permit is obtained when the employer applies through the e-permit system using the foreign national's identity number or reference number.

Under Turkish legislation, two different procedures apply to obtaining a work permit, depending on whether the application is made from within Türkiye or from abroad. These procedures are examined in detail below.

Domestic Work Permit Application

A domestic work permit application is made when the foreign national is in Türkiye and holds a residence permit valid for at least 6 months. These persons have a foreign identity number starting with 99. The employer applies through the e-permit system for the foreign national to be employed using this identity number.

Overseas Work Permit Application

An overseas work permit application is made when the foreign national is abroad and does not hold a residence permit valid for at least 6 months. These foreign nationals must first apply to the Turkish diplomatic mission in their country of nationality for a work visa. Upon the application, a 16-digit reference number is assigned to the foreign national. The employer applies through the e-permit system for the foreign national to be employed using this reference number.

Work Permit Application Steps

Regardless of whether the application follows the domestic or overseas procedure, it must be made by the employer through the e-permit system. The steps to be followed in an application made through the e-permit system are as follows:

  • First, the criteria that workplaces must meet to employ foreign nationals should be reviewed on the Ministry's website. If these criteria are met, the application may begin.
  • Next, it should be checked whether the SGK e-notification user who will register the workplace in the Ministry's automation system has an electronic signature in his or her own name.
  • Before starting the application, an employment contract must be signed with the foreign national planned to be employed. Sample employment contracts are available on the Ministry's website (for overseas applications, this contract must have been signed in advance by the parties and submitted to the diplomatic mission when requesting a work visa).
  • Before proceeding to the foreign work permit application, the e-notification user must enter the Ministry's foreign work permit automation system and create a workplace registration. Workplace registration is completed by electronically signing the undertaking that opens after the required information and documents are entered.
  • After workplace registration is created, the e-notification user or a person authorized by him or her may apply for a foreign work permit with an e-signature through that workplace.
  • After entering the "Apply" tab in the left menu of the e-permit application, the application option corresponding to the foreign national's status and situation must be selected, and the information and documents requested in the following tabs must be completed step by step until all tabs are finished. (A tab whose information has been fully completed can be identified by the green check mark next to the tab title.)
  • After all information and documents have been entered, at the final stage the application may be saved or approved. If the petition, application form and undertaking that open when the approve button is clicked are signed with an electronic signature, the application is completed and reaches the Ministry for evaluation.
  • During the evaluation process, the Ministry may provide information by e-mail when necessary. The current status of the application may also be checked by entering the "Application Tracking" tab in the left menu of the e-permit application.
  • If the application is evaluated positively by the Ministry, the applicant is informed by e-mail to pay the required fees. For work permit applications made from abroad, the required fee, valuable paper charge and other payments must be paid in person by the foreign national at the relevant diplomatic mission.
  • Work permit applications for which fees and valuable paper charges have been paid are approved by the Ministry and converted into work permits, and the printed work permit cards are sent by PTT courier to the workplace address.
  • For applications made from within Türkiye, SGK insured entry must be made within 30 days following the work permit start date; for applications made from abroad, within 30 days from the foreign national's date of entry into the country, at least at the wage declared to the Ministry. This is mandatory.

ATTENTION: Foreign nationals who enter Türkiye with a work visa obtained from Turkish diplomatic missions abroad must register their address at the nearest provincial directorate general of migration within at most 20 business days from the date of entry into Türkiye.

Foreign Work Permit Inquiry

Foreign work permit inquiry is made through the Ministry of Labour and Social Security website. Through this system, foreign nationals' work permits and work permit exemptions may be queried.

On the screen that opens, "Yabancı Çalışma İzni" (Foreign Work Permit) is selected in the section "Select the Application Type You Wish to Query". Then the "Foreign Identity Number/Reference Number" and "Application Number" are entered in the relevant fields to query the application.

Ministry Evaluation and Finalisation Process

The Ministry of Labour and Social Security evaluates and finalises foreign work permit applications, where necessary obtaining the views of relevant public institutions and organisations. Foreign work permit applications made in accordance with the procedure are finalised by the Ministry within at most 30 days, provided the documents are complete.

If it is determined that the application was made with incomplete documents, the applicant is informed that the missing documents must be completed. In that case, the 30-day period starts from the date the missing documents are submitted to the Ministry.

The Ministry notifies its positive or negative decision on the foreign work permit to the relevant diplomatic mission for notification to the foreign applicant in overseas applications. In domestic applications, the employer is notified.

ru.title: Типы разрешений на работу
ru.content:
Types of work permit are regulated in the International Labour Force Law. Under the Law, there are five types of work permit: temporary work permit, indefinite work permit, independent work permit, exceptional work permit and Turquoise Card.

Temporary Work Permit

A temporary work permit is a work permit granted for at most 1 year on first application, not exceeding the term of the employment or service contract, on condition of working at a specific workplace belonging to a real or legal person or public institution or organisation, or at workplaces in the same sector, in a specific job.

Article 10/1 of the International Labour Force Law regulates the temporary work permit as follows:

"If the application is evaluated positively, the foreign national is granted a work permit valid for at most 1 year on first application, not exceeding the term of the employment or service contract, on condition of working at a specific workplace belonging to a real or legal person or public institution or organisation, or at workplaces in the same sector, in a specific job."

An extension application may also be made for a temporary work permit. If the extension application is concluded positively, the foreign national may be granted a foreign work permit for at most 2 years on the first extension application and at most 3 years on subsequent extension applications, while remaining with the same employer.

Indefinite Work Permit

An indefinite work permit is a type of work permit that grants the foreign national the right to work indefinitely in Türkiye. Foreign nationals with a long-term residence permit in Türkiye or at least 8 years of lawful work permit may apply for an indefinite work permit.

Indefinite work permit documents are renewed at the end of every 5 years from the work permit start date. The renewal application must be made within the 6 months before the end of the 5-year period from the start of the indefinite work permit and in any case before the period expires. Foreign nationals with an indefinite work permit may not work in jobs and professions prohibited to them by special regulations and reserved only for Turkish citizens.

Independent Work Permit

An independent work permit is a type of work permit that grants the foreign national the right to work on his or her own account in Türkiye. This permit is granted to foreign professional practitioners provided the special conditions set out in other laws are met. The independent work permit is issued for a limited period, but no specific duration is prescribed.

For more detailed information on what an independent work permit is, its conditions, how it is obtained and which documents are required, you may read our article on "Independent Work Permit".

Exceptional Work Permit

An exceptional work permit is a work permit granted to persons listed in Article 16 of the International Labour Force Law in line with labour force policies determined by the Ministry.

The foreign nationals listed below may apply for an exceptional work permit.

  • Those evaluated as qualified labour because of their education level, wage, professional experience, contribution to science and technology, etc.,
  • Those evaluated as qualified investors because of their contribution to science and technology, level of investment and exports, size of employment to be provided, etc.,
  • Those employed by their employer in a project carried out in Türkiye for a specific period,
  • Those notified by the Ministry of Interior or Ministry of Foreign Affairs as being of Turkish descent,
  • TRNC citizens,
  • EU member country citizens,
  • International protection applicants, conditional refugees, persons under temporary protection, stateless persons or victims of human trafficking benefiting from victim support procedures,
  • Those married to a Turkish citizen and living in marital union with their spouse in Türkiye,
  • Those working at representations of foreign states and international organisations in Türkiye without diplomatic immunity,
  • Those coming to Türkiye for scientific, cultural, artistic or sporting purposes and internationally renowned for their achievements in their field,
  • Cross-border service provider foreign nationals.

For more detailed information on what an exceptional work permit is, which criteria must be met to obtain it and who may obtain an exceptional work permit, you may read our article on "exceptional work permit".

Turquoise Card

The Turquoise Card is a card granting indefinite residence and work permit to persons who will contribute to Türkiye as qualified labour, through professional experience or in various other ways. The card also grants indefinite residence rights to the foreign national's spouse and children under 18 or children in need of special care.

The Turquoise Card is issued with the first 3 years as a transition period. During this period the Ministry may request necessary information and documents from the employer or the foreign national. If the Turquoise Card is not cancelled during the transition period, the transition period record on the card is removed upon the foreign national's application and an indefinite Turquoise Card is issued.

Foreign nationals holding a Turquoise Card benefit from the rights provided by the indefinite work permit regulated in the International Labour Force Law. The rights provided by the Turquoise Card are as follows:

  • They are exempt from military service in Türkiye.
  • They may not benefit from electoral rights or the right to hold public office.
  • Acquired social security rights are reserved, and use of these rights is subject to the relevant legislation.
  • Procedures regarding residence, travel, work, investment, commercial activity, inheritance, acquisition and transfer of movable and immovable property in Türkiye are carried out by the relevant institutions and organisations under the legislation applied to Turkish citizens.
  • If special laws require Turkish citizenship to use these rights and obligations, persons holding a Turquoise Card may not claim these rights.
  • Under Article 12(1)(b) of Law No. 5901 on Turkish Citizenship, Turquoise Card holders and their relatives may acquire Turkish citizenship upon proposal by the Ministry if there is no situation threatening national security or public order and the transition period record is removed.

For more detailed information on what the Turquoise Card is, how it is obtained, the required conditions and necessary documents, you may read our article titled "turquoise card".

ru.title: Условия получения разрешения на работу иностранцами
ru.content:
Conditions for foreign nationals to obtain a work permit consist of meeting the Ministry's evaluation criteria. These criteria must be met by both the foreign employee and the employer. In this scope, the conditions for foreign nationals to obtain a work permit are as follows:

  • At the workplace for which a work permit is requested, at least 5 Turkish citizens must be employed. If the foreign national requesting a work permit is a company partner, the five-employee requirement applies for the last 6 months of the one-year work permit to be granted by the Ministry. If work permit requests are made for more than one foreign national at the same workplace, 5 Turkish citizens must be employed separately for each foreign national after the first foreign national granted a work permit.
  • The workplace's paid-in capital must be at least 100,000 TL, gross sales at least 800,000 TL, or last year's export amount at least 250,000 US Dollars.
  • For permit requests relating to foreign nationals working in associations and foundations, Article 2 does not apply; for work permit applications of foreign nationals to work at representations of foreign state airlines, in the education sector and in domestic services, Articles 1 and 2 do not apply.
  • For a foreign company partner applying for a work permit, the capital share must be at least 20 percent and not less than 40,000 TL.
  • The monthly wage to be paid to the foreign national declared by the employer must be commensurate with the foreign national's duty and competence. Accordingly, taking into account the minimum wage in force on the application date, the wage to be paid to the foreign national must be at least;
    • 6.5 times the minimum wage for senior executives and pilots,
    • 4 times the minimum wage for unit or branch managers, engineers and architects,
    • 3 times the minimum wage for those working in jobs requiring expertise and craftsmanship and for teachers,
    • at least the minimum wage for foreign nationals employed in domestic services, and 1.5 times the minimum wage for foreign nationals working in other professions,
    • 2 times the minimum wage for foreign nationals working as acrobats and in similar titles at tourism-animation organisation firms and for masseurs, masseuses and SPA therapists.
  • Among workplaces that;
    • Are certified tourism enterprises with at least three stars documented by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism proving they have a licensed massage salon, certified holiday villages, or thermal hotels with operating permits from official authorities,
    • Are certified tourism enterprises with hamam-sauna-SPA complexes or contracted facilities (with a contract),
    • Are officially licensed sports centres employing at least 20 Turkish citizens,
    • Requests to employ foreign nationals in jobs requiring expertise and craftsmanship such as masseur, masseuse and SPA therapist will be evaluated; requests from workplaces and enterprises not within this scope will not be approved.
  • For foreign nationals to be employed in jobs requiring expertise and craftsmanship in the entertainment sector and tourism-animation organisation firms, if at least 10 Turkish citizens are employed, the separate quota of 5 Turkish citizens for each foreign national will not additionally apply.
  • For work permit requests relating to foreign nationals to be employed under bilateral or multilateral agreements to which Türkiye is party and in procurement of goods and services by public institutions through contract or tender procedures, the criteria in Articles 1 and 2 will not apply.
  • In jobs requiring advanced technology or where no Turkish specialist with the same qualifications is available, upon approval by the General Directorate, the criteria in Articles 1 and 2 will not apply.
  • For foreign nationals to be employed in enterprises with Characteristic Direct Foreign Investment conditions other than key personnel, the criterion in Article 1 is applied based on the number of Turkish citizens employed at all workplaces of the enterprise nationwide.
Exceptions to the Conditions

There are also foreign nationals not subject to the evaluation criteria listed above. However, even if exempt from the evaluation criteria, these foreign nationals must obtain a work permit to work in Türkiye. Foreign nationals exempt from evaluation criteria are as follows:

  • Foreign nationals whose mother, father or child is a Turkish citizen,
  • Foreign nationals who have lived in marital union with a Turkish citizen for at least 3 years,
  • TRNC citizens,
  • Foreign nationals granted residence permits under Turkish or kin community arrangements,
  • Foreign nationals granted humanitarian residence permits,
  • Foreign nationals granted residence permits as victims of human trafficking,
  • Foreign nationals granted residence permits with stateless status are exempt from evaluation criteria.

ru.title: Документы для иностранного разрешения на работу
ru.content:
The documents required for a foreign work permit are as follows:

  • Employment contract signed by the employer and the foreign national,
  • Passport copy,
    • If the passport is not written in Latin letters, a sworn translator's or officially approved translation must also be attached to the application.
    • Under Article 23 of Law No. 6458, work permits to be issued to foreign nationals whose request is found appropriate by the Ministry of Labour and Social Security are arranged not to exceed the date 60 days before the passport expiry date. Work permit applications made with a passport or passport substitute document valid for less than 60 days on the application date are not processed.
  • Diploma or Provisional Graduation Certificate copy with Turkish translation approved by a sworn translator or official authorities,
    • A diploma is mandatory for foreign nationals who will work in professional services and in professions required by the Ministry. For domestic services, submitting a diploma is not mandatory; a declaration regarding the last school completed is sufficient.
  • Trade Registry Gazette of Türkiye showing the enterprise's latest capital and partnership structure,
  • Balance sheet and profit/loss statement for the last year, approved by the tax office or a sworn certified public accountant.

The information and documents listed above are common requirements for all types of work permit. Together with these documents, separate information and document uploads are required according to the sectors in which the foreign national wishes to work in Türkiye. These sectors and the documents required by sector are explained separately below.

Documents Required for Entertainment Sector Work Permit

The documents required for an entertainment sector work permit application are as follows:

  • Portfolio (Bonservis) with Turkish translation approved by a sworn translator or official authorities (the portfolio of the foreign national for whom a work permit is requested must bear an apostille stamp or diplomatic mission certification showing international renown as an artist or equivalent experience performing programmes at foreign enterprises of the same level),
  • Employment contract in Turkish and in the foreign national's language (the employment contract must bear the wet signatures of the employer and the foreign national),
  • Operating Certificate obtained from the Ministry of Culture and Tourism.

There are also mandatory conditions that must appear in employment contracts with foreign artists. These mandatory conditions are as follows:

  • A record undertaking that return tickets and travel expenses will be covered by the employer when foreign artists return to their countries after their working periods,
  • An undertaking that the wage may not be lower than 3 times the minimum wage, which changes every 6 months,
  • Workplace Tax Number,
  • In addition to the employee's rights, the numbers 155 Police Emergency and 157 Human Trafficking Victims Helpline, Alo 170 helpline and contact telephones of our Ministry's Provincial Directorates of Labour and Employment Agency when consultation is needed.

For more information on what the entertainment sector is, which foreign nationals may apply for this work permit and the required conditions, you may read our article on "entertainment sector work permit".

Aviation Sector Work Permit

The documents required for an aviation sector work permit are as follows:

  • Pilot Licence with Turkish translation approved by a sworn translator or official authorities,
  • The work permit to be issued by the Ministry of Labour and Social Security becomes valid together with the Validation Certificate to be obtained from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation of the Ministry of Transport to validate foreign pilots' licences in Türkiye.

ATTENTION: The aviation sector work permit to be issued by the Ministry becomes valid together with the Validation Certificate to be obtained from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation of the Ministry of Transport to validate foreign pilots' licences in Türkiye.

General information on work permits for the aviation sector is provided under this heading. For detailed information on obtaining a work permit to work in the aviation sector, you may read our article titled "aviation sector work permit".

Key Personnel

The documents required to apply for a key personnel work permit are as follows:

  • Information and documents showing that the company or branch is "characteristic direct foreign investment",
  • Information and documents showing that the foreign personnel is key personnel,
  • Documents showing that foreign exchange was brought from abroad within the last year for liaison office activities,
  • Foreign Personnel Notification Form,
  • Foreign national's employment acceptance certificate or certified copy,
  • Passport copy and translation,
  • Curriculum vitae form,
  • Work permit request petition.

More detailed information on who key personnel are, how a key personnel work permit may be obtained, the amount of characteristic direct investment and how to apply for this type of work permit appears in our article on "key personnel work permit".

Liaison Offices

The documents required for work permit applications made by liaison offices are as follows:

  • Operating permit documents (must be obtained from the relevant ministry for foreign nationals to be employed in liaison offices),
  • Documents showing that at least 200 thousand US Dollars or equivalent foreign exchange was brought from abroad within the last year for liaison offices (such as authority certificate for the office manager and bank receipt, bank letter, foreign exchange purchase document copy relating to foreign exchange transfer).
Work Permit for Foreign Company Partners

The documents required in applications for work permits by foreign company partners are as follows:

  • Passport copy,
  • Diploma or Provisional Graduation Certificate copy with Turkish translation approved by a sworn translator or official authorities,
  • Trade Registry Gazette of Türkiye showing the enterprise's latest capital and partnership structure,
  • Balance sheet and profit/loss statement for the last year, approved by the tax office or a sworn certified public accountant.

For more detailed information on how foreign company partners may obtain a work permit, the conditions and which partners must or need not obtain this work permit, you may read our article on "work permit for foreign company partners".

Tourism Sector Work Permit

The documents required for tourism sector work permit applications are as follows:

  • Operating and Investment Certificate from the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, or if not a certified enterprise, Activity Certificate from the Chamber of Commerce,
  • The number of foreign personnel employed in tourism enterprises may not exceed 10% of total personnel. This ratio may be increased by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism to 20%. Therefore, under Article 18 of Law No. 2634 on Encouragement of Tourism, employment of at least five Turkish citizens at that workplace is mandatory for each foreign national for whom a work permit is requested.

For detailed information on how to obtain a foreign work permit for the tourism sector, criteria for employing foreign personnel in the tourism sector and points to consider when drafting employment contracts with foreign nationals in this sector, you may read our article on "tourism sector work permit".

Foreign Doctor Work Permit

The documents required for foreign doctor work permit applications are as follows:

  • Pre-authorisation document (for foreign health professionals to work in private health institutions affiliated to the Ministry of Health, obtained from the provincial health directorate of the province where the health institution is located, showing the foreign national's professional competence),
  • Operating permit document (private health institutions wishing to employ foreign doctors or other health workers may obtain this from the provincial health directorate).
  • Diploma equivalence certificate if the foreign national graduated from faculties abroad.

Decree Law No. 663 enabled foreign doctors and nurses to work in Türkiye. Therefore, private health institutions employing foreign doctors/nurses may apply to the Ministry for a work permit together with the pre-authorisation (professional competence) document obtained from the provincial health directorate. If the foreign national for whom a work permit is requested graduated from faculties abroad, submission of a diploma equivalence certificate is mandatory.

For more detailed information on foreign doctor work permit criteria, how the pre-authorisation process works and documents required for pre-authorisation application, you may read our article on "foreign doctor work permit".

Foreign Caregiver Work Permit

Applications for foreign caregiver work permits to employ foreign personnel in domestic services have increased recently. To prevent abuse of this permit type and for the security of foreign nationals granted work permits, the Ministry has introduced certain limitations listed below.

  • It is not possible to grant work permits to foreign nationals for domestic services other than care of the elderly, sick and children.
  • It is mandatory to prove with a health board report that the employer has a condition requiring care.
  • Except in serious cases requiring intensive care, work permits are not granted to male foreign nationals in residences.

The documents required for a foreign caregiver work permit are as follows:

  • Employment contract signed by the employer and the foreign national (for overseas applications, this contract must have been signed in advance by the parties and submitted by the foreign personnel to Turkish diplomatic missions when requesting a work visa),
  • Passport copy,
  • For domestic services, submitting a diploma is not mandatory; a declaration regarding the last school completed is sufficient.
  • Employer's identity card,
  • Identity card of the person to be cared for (if the person to be cared for is elderly, a health certificate or board report must also be obtained),
  • Employer's population registry sample,
  • Detailed population registry sample of the elderly, sick or child,
  • Document showing the employer's income status,
  • If a first-degree relative is the employer, a document showing the relationship is also required.

More detailed information on what a foreign caregiver work permit is, how it is obtained, criteria for employing foreign caregivers and points to consider in employment contracts appears in our article on "foreign caregiver work permit".

Foreign Architect and Engineer Work Permit

The documents required for a foreign architect and engineer work permit are as follows:

  • For foreign nationals requesting work permits as engineers and architects within professional services who received higher education abroad, "Diploma or Provisional Graduation Equivalence Certificate" to be obtained in accordance with the relevant legislation,
  • Legal entities employing foreign specialists as engineers/architects/urban planners must submit payroll proving employment of a Turkish national in the same profession.

General information on foreign architect and engineer work permits is provided under this heading. For detailed information on obtaining work permits for foreign architects and engineers, you may read our article titled "foreign architect and engineer work permit".

Foreign Student Work Permit

Foreign students enrolled in formal education programmes at a higher education institution in Türkiye may work provided they have a work permit. Associate degree, undergraduate, graduate and doctoral students in our country may apply for a foreign student work permit after completing the first year of their studies.

The documents required for a foreign student work permit are as follows:

  • Employment contract signed by the employer and the foreign national (for overseas applications, this contract must have been signed in advance by the parties and submitted by the foreign national to Turkish diplomatic missions when requesting a work visa),
  • Trade Registry Gazette of Türkiye showing the enterprise's latest capital and partnership structure,
  • Balance sheet and profit/loss statement for the last year, approved by the tax office or a sworn certified public accountant.

The documents required from the foreign student for a foreign student work permit are as follows:

  • Passport copy,
  • Biometric photograph,
  • Student certificate.

General information on foreign student work permits is provided under this heading. For detailed information on obtaining a foreign student work permit, you may read our article titled "foreign student work permit".

Must a Foreign Student Obtain a Work Permit for Internship?

A foreign student must apply for work permit exemption for internships that are mandatory under university education.

Under Article 48/1-n of the International Labour Force Implementation Regulation, foreign students enrolled in a formal education programme in Türkiye who are required by the relevant legislation to intern with an employer within vocational training are evaluated within work permit exemption for the mandatory internship period.

Foreign Teacher Work Permit

The documents required for a foreign teacher work permit application are as follows:

  • For foreign nationals to work at private educational institutions affiliated to the Ministry of National Education, a document from MEB showing the foreign national's professional competence (pre-authorisation document),
  • For private educational institutions employing foreign nationals, "Institution Opening and Commencement of Education Permit" and "Licence" obtained from MEB are among the documents required for a foreign teacher work permit.

For detailed information on how a foreign teacher work permit is obtained, conditions for foreign teachers to obtain a work permit and how the MEB pre-authorisation process works, you may read our article on "foreign teacher work permit".

ru.title: На что обратить внимание в трудовых договорах с иностранцами
ru.content:
Points to consider in employment contracts with foreign personnel are as follows:

  • The employment contract to be signed between the foreign national and the employer must comply with the Labour Law and other legislation,
  • The wage to be paid to the foreign national in the employment contract must not be below the mandatory minimum wages specified in the Ministry's evaluation criteria (these wages are explained in a subsection below),
  • Depending on the sectors in which the foreign national will work, if recruitment was made according to the person's qualifications, he or she must be employed in an appropriate job, and necessary arrangements must be made in the employment contract where required.

ru.title: Обязательная минимальная заработная плата для иностранцев
ru.content:
The wage determined for foreign personnel must be commensurate with the foreign national's duty and competence. Accordingly, taking into account the minimum wage in force on the application date, the wage to be paid to the foreign national must be at least the amounts specified below.

  • 6.5 times the minimum wage for senior executives and pilots (from 01.01.2023 gross 65,052.00 TL),
  • 4 times the minimum wage for unit or branch managers, engineers and architects (from 01.01.2023 gross 40,032.00 TL),
  • 3 times the minimum wage for those working in jobs requiring expertise and craftsmanship and for teachers (from 01.01.2023 gross 30,024.00 TL),
  • at least the minimum wage for foreign nationals employed in domestic services (from 01.01.2023 gross 10,008.00 TL), and 1.5 times the minimum wage for foreign nationals working in other professions (from 01.01.2023 gross 15,012.00 TL),
  • 2 times the minimum wage for foreign nationals working as acrobats and in similar titles at tourism-animation organisation firms and for masseurs, masseuses and SPA therapists (from 01.01.2023 gross 20,016.00 TL).

The wage to be paid to the foreign national must be correctly stated in the employment contract according to the various professions listed above. Arranging the wage to be paid to the foreign national below these amounts in the employment contract is grounds for rejection of the work permit application.

ru.title: Какие профессии не могут получить разрешение на работу?
ru.content:
It is not possible to grant work permits to foreign nationals in professions and duties reserved only for Turkish citizens in the relevant laws. Accordingly, professions for which work permits cannot be obtained are as follows:

  • Founders, Managers, Trainers of Private Security Companies and Representatives Authorized by the Corporate Partner of the Company,
  • Private Security Officers,
  • Market and Neighbourhood Watchmanship,
  • Certified Public Accountancy,
  • Cooperative Board Members,
  • Customs Broker Assistant,
  • Founders of Schools Teaching in Languages Other Than Turkish and Opened by Foreign Nationals,
  • Responsible Manager in Private Hospitals,
  • Dentistry, Patient Care,
  • Pharmacy,
  • Veterinary Medicine,
  • Foreign Assistants Working Outside Speciality Training,
  • Notary,
  • Judgeship and Prosecution,
  • Legal Practice,
  • Mediation,
  • Expert Witness,
  • Concordat Commissariat,
  • Trainee Aviation Information Management Officer,
  • Honorary Traffic Inspector,
  • Freight Forwarding Organisation,
  • Agency Manager, Travel Agency Manager,
  • Tourist Guiding,
  • Export of Fish, Oyster, Mussel, Sponge, Pearl, Coral within Territorial Waters, Diving, Searching, Pilotage, Captaincy, Net Fishing, Clerkship, Deckhand etc.,
  • Sports Consultancy,
  • Job Placement in Agriculture,
  • Ship Agency Officer and Ship Agency Personnel,
  • Permanent Supervisor, Technical Officer.

Jobs and professions that only Turkish citizens may perform under various laws and regulations are listed above. Foreign nationals may not apply for foreign work permits in these occupational fields.

ru.title: Освобождения от разрешения на работу
ru.content:
Work permit exemption refers to the document granting the right to work and reside in Türkiye without obtaining a work permit. Persons who may apply for work permit exemption are listed in Article 48 of the International Labour Force Law Implementation Regulation. According to the Regulation, persons who may obtain work permit exemption and exemption periods are as follows:

  • Up to 1 month for foreign nationals who will work in science, culture and art,
  • Up to 3 months for foreign nationals who will provide training on goods and services exported from or imported to Türkiye or on use, maintenance or repair of machinery and systems imported to Türkiye,
  • Up to 3 months for foreign nationals residing abroad determined by ministries as being of Turkish descent,
  • Up to 3 months for those working in sports activities,
  • Up to 4 months for foreign nationals who will intern within university international student exchange programmes (Erasmus, AIESEC, Farabi etc.), up to 12 months if these exchange programmes are approved by the General Directorate of International Labour Force,
  • Up to 6 months for foreign nationals who will work in seasonal agriculture and livestock jobs determined by the General Directorate of International Labour Force,
  • Up to 6 months for foreign nationals declared by relevant public institutions and organisations to make significant contributions to Türkiye in economy, socio-cultural matters, technology or education,
  • Up to 8 months for foreign nationals who will work as tour operator representatives,
  • Up to six months for foreign nationals who will work at fairs and circuses operating outside the boundaries of certified tourism enterprises,
  • With approval of the Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Turkish Football Federation, for foreign athletes, coaches, physiotherapists, masseurs and other personnel who enter Türkiye with a sports-based visa, for the duration of their contracts with sports clubs in Türkiye,
  • For those working in Türkiye within the scope of financial cooperation agreements between Türkiye and the European Union, for the duration of their employment,
  • For foreign seafarers on ships registered in the Turkish International Ship Registry working outside the cabotage line, until the employment contract ends,
  • For foreign university students enrolled in a formal education programme in Türkiye with mandatory internship, for the internship period,
  • For those who are civil servants at diplomatic or consular missions of foreign countries in Türkiye for the duration of their duties, and for those working under employment contracts until the contract ends,
  • For foreign nationals working at schools, cultural institutions and religious institutions operating as affiliated units of diplomatic and consular missions of foreign countries in Türkiye, for the duration of their duties,
  • For foreign nationals coming to Türkiye for TUS or DUS, for the duration of their education,
  • Up to 1 month for cross-border service providers,
  • Up to 3 months for foreign board members of joint stock companies who do not reside in Türkiye,
  • For foreign nationals specialising in medicine or dentistry, for the duration of their education,
  • For foreign personnel, researchers or managers who will work within the Turkish-Japanese University of Science and Technology, for the duration of their employment contracts,
  • Up to 3 months for non-managing foreign partners of companies other than joint stock companies,
  • Work permit exemption may be granted to those working in factories or shipyards under the Ministry of National Defence or under MKE for the duration of their employment contracts.

The documents required for work permit exemption are as follows:

  • Biometric photograph of the foreign national,
  • Valid passport or passport substitute document,
  • Education and, if any, workplace information and supporting documents.

General information on work permit exemptions is provided under this heading. For detailed information on work permit exemptions, you may read our article titled "work permit exemption".

ru.title: Разрешения на работу для сирийцев
ru.content:
Work permits for Syrians are evaluated within work permit applications for foreign nationals under temporary protection. Rules on Syrians under temporary protection working in Türkiye are regulated in the Regulation on Work Permits of Foreigners Under Temporary Protection.

Conditions for Syrians to obtain a work permit are as follows:

  • The Syrian person must have a temporary protection identity document and a foreign identity number starting with 99. The foreign identity number starting with 99 is issued with the temporary protection identity document.
  • As of the application date, the Syrian person must have been in Türkiye for at least 6 months under temporary protection.
  • For professions requiring pre-authorisation such as teaching, medicine and academia, a pre-authorisation document must be obtained from the Ministry of National Education, Ministry of Health or Council of Higher Education.
  • The application must not relate to professions permitted only to Turkish citizens.
  • The application must be made for one of the jobs the Ministry of Labour and Social Security permits foreigners under temporary protection to perform.
  • Provincial and employment quota conditions must be met at the workplace where Syrians under temporary protection will be employed.

Detailed information on conditions for Syrians to obtain work permits, how they may obtain them, Ministry evaluation criteria and employment quotas appears in our article on "Syrian work permit".

ru.title: Разрешения на работу для лиц турецкого происхождения
ru.content:
Foreign nationals notified by the Ministry of Interior or Ministry of Foreign Affairs as being of Turkish descent may apply to work in occupational and artistic fields needed in Türkiye for jobs reserved for Turkish citizens. However, they may work in these occupational and artistic fields at public, private or workplace establishments, except the Turkish Armed Forces and Security Organisation.

General information on work permit documents for foreign nationals of Turkish descent is provided under this heading. For detailed information on work permits for foreign nationals of Turkish descent, you may read our article titled "Turkish descent work permit".
